Rechargeable wireless mouse and keyboard combo, and it lights up! So fun, I never knew I needed this until I got one. My last keyboard was a retro-style typewriter and lit up but it went awry when the keys kept skipping my keystrokes. This keyboard types like a dream, it is a little tactile and noisy but not as much as the typewriter-style one was. The lighting is pretty, I enjoy seeing all my letters and numbers lit while typing in the dark so if I ever need to look I can, even though I know how to type most of the time it is the numbers and symbols I don't have all of them memorized. Not everyone gets a keyboarding class in school, but I recommend it to everyone if they get the chance to learn to type without looking it really helps a lot. Everything is going to be tech and less on paper anymore. Might as well make the best of it. I sure miss the days of pretty cursive. A lit keyboard sure is nice though. The mouse works wonderfully too. both use the same charging cord, there is an optional type c adapter if needed. Keep it in a safe place you never know when you might need those adapter things. F and J have the placement bumps so you can find your correct placement. The most important thing for me is that it has a volume button I can push up and down on without holding down the function key with the plus or minus button. Less hassle. Not a lot of keyboards have this, and the more expensive ones have a knob sometimes. If you have used this speaker's plus or minus buttons (without the function key needed), you never go back. Instantly changes volume in a flash, sometimes I leave it up after a movie and forget and then have to quickly lower the volume so as to not disturb the peace much. Oops! There is also a quick mute button to hit in that case as well. I thoroughly enjoy my new keyboard and hope it lasts for years to come.

I’ve been on a quest to find the best (perfect would be nice but....) TWE’s in the sub $150 price range. I mainly use them for watching TV, listening to audiobooks while riding my bike and podcasts and some music (I have dedicated IEM’s for serious music listening). I began my search with the Soundcore series by Anker because I’ve used their other products for years and I find their quality to be above average for the money. My first foray into the TWE world were the Soundcore Life A1’s. I still have them and for the money they are hard to beat. Small, comfortable, great battery life and minuscule pill case charger. Also used them for a phone call and they were great for that, but I almost never talk on the phone so .......Next we’re the Soundcore Life A2 NC because I wanted to try noise cancelling. I didn’t really NEED NC but I thought it would reduce wind noise while riding. It didn’t. They also were impossible to get securely in my weird ears. I tried all the different tips and wings but the would fall out on occasion (once into the compost pile while turning that monster). So they went back in favor of these Liberty 2 Pro’s. Initially I was very disappointed. The gimmicky “10 Grammy Winner” EQ settings are ridiculous. And as with all the TWE’s so far none of them give me the volume my 70 year old ears need, but at least these come with the option to run the EQ up to +6 dB across the board so that helps with the casual listening thing. They also came with ear tips perhaps best for a large mouse or maybe a small cat and there was no chance the would stay in so I changed them to a larger set (there are 7 sizes to choose from, all silicone 😢) and they fit better now. They are substantially heavier than the Life A1’s but we’ll see how secure they are as time goes by. I do wish they would offer some foam tip options and I’ll be trying out some Delkoni tips in the near future. As for the Astoria Aural Coaxial Architecture thing, they sound pretty good. Not BGVP DM6 good, but not bad for Bluetooth. The AptX is decent, pairing was simple, the wireless charging is nice, and the packaging was phenomenal for the price. I went for the refurbished set and I can’t tell them from brand spanking new. There really isn’t anywhere else to go with the Soundcore line so we’ll see. Updates coming if things change.

This also works on any OTG-capable phone using her approach because I tested it on my Galaxy Note 3.

A big plus is this not only works with USB 3.0 interfaces, but is backward compatible to earlier versions of the USB spec, including 1.0. That means that I can use this on my legacy devices around the house, as well as my newer 'toys'.

The final thing that I like about this hub is the construction. The manufacturer did not cut corners on cable gauge and the small details like strain relief, precision made connectors and other areas that cheaper brands do. The quality is there and this does work as advertised.

I received a expensive digital camera for Christmas and then promptly freaked everyone out as I don't like straps. After dropping it a couple of times, I started looking for straps I could live with and came across This grip camera case. That's all I use now and I leave the cumbersome camera bag in the car while I am taking photographs. It adapts to any DSLR camera as there is a grid of holes that you screw the main piece onto. Once you have done that the whole piece fits and closes your camera to the elements and it's made of a neoprene material that takes some pretty good shock if you do drop it. However, once you slid it off your lens, there is a cuff that you slide onto your wrist, adjust the stretch drawstring to securing fasten. You are now free to drop your camera and it ends up hanging off your wrist. I have a telephoto lense and this works with both.
The feature I really like is the fact that you can slide your lense cover into the front which houses your lense. I have not lost a lense cover since. It comes in a series of different designs to fit both men's and women's tastes.
